questions.q: What started Allen's long spiral of anxious thinking?
a: A man threatened her after a talk, then a power outage
A divorce and a sudden move to another city
Losing her job at a Baptist church
A serious illness in her immediate family
questions.why: The first lesson says the threat and the strange outage made her anxious for the next 18 months.

questions.q: What finally helped Allen begin to recover?
a: Thinking about her thoughts from an outside view
Avoiding church for several months
Asking a doctor for medication
Writing a book about demons
questions.why: The first lesson says she began to think about her thinking and saw she could choose which thoughts to keep.

questions.q: What does the summary say meditation does for you?
a: It rewires your thinking patterns to be healthier
It removes your need for sleep
It erases painful memories
It builds willpower permanently
questions.why: The second lesson cites science showing that solitude and meditation can change the brain for the better.

questions.q: What does Allen suggest replacing the why at the end of a thought with?
a: An action statement beginning with so I will
A question about what caused the feeling
A promise to try harder next time
A reminder to stay calm and breathe
questions.why: The second lesson says this phrase moves you from a reactive mindset to a proactive one.

questions.q: What does the summary say about asking others for help?
a: It is strength, not weakness, and connection defeats toxic thoughts
It should only be a last resort after self-help
It works mainly for outgoing people
It can make negative thinking worse
questions.why: The third lesson says being known and loved by good people is what keeps toxic thinking at bay.
